text: Miss World is the oldest existing international beauty pageant, founded in 1951 in the United Kingdom by Eric Morley. Morley organized a bikini contest as part of the Festival of Britain celebrations, which was later dubbed "Miss World" by the press. The swimsuit competition was intended to promote the newly introduced bikini, which was still considered immodest, and when Kerstin "Kiki" Hakansson of Sweden was crowned in a bikini in 1951, it sparked controversy, leading to religious objections and a papal condemnation. As a result, the bikini was replaced in future pageants with more modest swimwear, and from 1976, evening gowns were used for crowning. Håkansson remains the only Miss World crowned in a bikini. Morley registered "Miss World" as a trademark and decided to make the pageant annual, though it was initially planned as a one-time Festival of Britain event. He announced winners in the order No. 3, No. 2, and No. 1 to maintain tension. The BBC began broadcasting the pageant in 1959, and it became one of the most watched programs in the UK during the 1960s and 1970s. In 1970, the London contest was disrupted by women's liberation protesters, and South Africa was banned due to sending two contestants, one black and one white. The pageant reached a peak viewership of over 18 million in the late 1970s and early 1980s. In the 1980s, it repositioned with the slogan "Beauty With a Purpose," adding intelligence and personality tests. In 1984, BBC1 controller Michael Grade announced it would cease broadcasting beauty pageants, calling them an anachronism. Thames Television aired the pageant from 1980 to 1988, after which ITV dropped it. Mainstream television broadcasts declined in the 1990s, and the pageant returned on Sky One in 1997 before moving to Channel 5 from 1998 to 2000. After Eric Morley's death in 2000, his widow Julia Morley became chair of the Miss World organization. The first black African Miss World winner, Agbani Darego of Nigeria, was crowned in 2001. That year, the organization launched a "Vote For Me" special, featuring delegates and allowing viewer voting, and also sold broadcasting rights for Talent, Beach Beauty, and Sports events. ITV broadcast the 2001 pageant from South Africa on digital channel ITV2, with the special airing a week earlier on main ITV. In 2002, the pageant was scheduled in Abuja, Nigeria, amid controversy over Amina Lawal, a woman awaiting stoning under Sharia law. The event faced boycotts from several nations including Denmark, Spain, Switzerland, Panama, Belgium, and Kenya, and protests led to inter-religious riots in Kaduna with over 200 deaths and destruction of religious sites. A fatwa calling for beheading of Isioma Daniel, who wrote a critical editorial, was issued but nullified by Saudi authorities. The pageant was moved to London due to safety concerns and the withdrawal of Canada and Korea, though many boycotting contestants later attended, including Kathrine Sørland of Norway. The eventual winner was Azra Akın of Turkey. In 2013, Islamic group protests led to the pageant being held in Hindu-majority Bali. Anastasia Lin of Canada missed the 2015 pageant due to a visa denial in China and was declared persona non grata for criticizing China's human rights; she later competed in 2016. The 2020 pageant was scheduled for Phuket, Thailand, but was canceled due to the global spread of COVID-19. The event was postponed indefinitely and later rescheduled to 16 December 2021, but due to positive cases among delegates—including Miss World Indonesia Carla Yules, Miss World India Manasa Varanasi, and Miss World Malaysia Lavanya Sivaji—the finale was postponed. On 15 December, 17 positive cases were confirmed in Puerto Rico, including contestants and staff, and on 16 December, Lavanya Sivaji tested positive and was isolated. The finale was ultimately held on 16 March 2022 at Puerto Rico's Coca-Cola Music Hall. Fast-track events, including Beauty With a Purpose (established in 1972), Talent (introduced in 1978), Sports (individual competition from 2006), Top Model (first held in 2004, resumed in 2007), and Multimedia (added in 2012), determine semi-finalist placements. Prior to 2016, fast-track winners earned points but did not guarantee a spot; since 2016, winners automatically qualify for quarter- or semi-finals. The Beach Beauty event, which ran from 2003 to 2015, was discontinued due to backlash from conservative countries and replaced the swimsuit competition, with a sarong introduced in 2013. The Miss World Organization manages the annual Miss World Finals, which has grown into one of the world's largest pageants, and since 1951 has raised over £1 billion for children's charities supporting disabled and underprivileged children. The pageant is franchised in more than 100 countries and has faced numerous controversies throughout its history.
